claims.claim: Generate a DME prescription from the Orders & DME module or directly within the Visit Wizard.
You must have prescribing authority or be creating the order on behalf of a supervising provider.
claims.finding: No prescribing-authority or supervising-provider check exists on the order path; the page is gated only by the Orders & DME feature (user-routes.tsx /patients/:patientId/orders). This is a policy statement, not product behaviour.

claims.claim: From the patient's chart open Orders & DME, or reach it from the Orders & DME section (section 12) of the Visit Wizard (the link carries the patient context automatically).
claims.finding: The chart has an Orders & DME tile (PatientOverviewPage.tsx:3571). The wizard step is badged "Step 11" (VisitWizardV4.tsx:18207) and embeds its own ordering panel (OrdersDMEVisit, :18233); it has no link to the Orders & DME page.
claims.proposed_text: From the patient's chart, click Orders & DME. During a visit you can also order from the Orders & DME step (Step 11) of the Visit Wizard, which works inside the wizard.

proposed_checks.note: the only Step 11 badge is the Orders & DME accordion (VisitWizardV4.tsx:18207)

claims.claim: Select the DME tab and click New DME Order.
claims.reason: With no DME orders yet, the button reads Create DME Order instead (PatientOrdersDmePage.tsx:1656).

claims.claim: Fill the DME order form top to bottom: select the Patient (type name or DOB, autocomplete); select Equipment Category (HCPCS codes filter by it); choose the Item (HCPCS populates automatically); set Quantity and Units; enter Duration; add Clinical Justification with an ICD-10 picker; select the Ordering Provider (NPI populates from profile); select the Vendor and optional custom form; add Notes.

checks.note: a free-text HCPCS box contradicts 'HCPCS populates automatically'

claims.finding: There is no fixed DME form with these fields. The flow is: New DME Order → "Select recipient for DME Order" (vendor first, :3750) → "Choose custom form" (:3857) → the chosen form. The patient is already set (page is per patient). The standard "Durable Medical Equipment Request" form (seed 20260924120000:162) has an Equipment checklist (Wheelchair, Walker, Hospital bed, ...), free-text "HCPCS code(s), if known", Quantity, "Length of need / start date", "Diagnosis / ICD-10 code(s)", "Ordering provider / credentials" and NPI. There is no equipment category, item picker, HCPCS auto-fill, units, or ICD-10 search; vendor forms vary.
claims.proposed_text: Click New DME Order, pick the vendor, then pick a form (the vendor's own, or the Medipyxis Durable Medical Equipment Request). Fill in the form: equipment, HCPCS codes if known, quantity, length of need, diagnosis / ICD-10 codes, and ordering provider and NPI.

claims.claim: Choose a supplier from the enabled-vendor list for DME. If the vendor has a custom order form, select it to capture vendor-specific fields.

checks.pattern: const vendorRows = await crmVendorService.list({ scopeFacilityId: facilityId });

claims.finding: The list is all of the clinic's enabled vendors plus home health agencies, not a DME-specific list (PatientOrdersDmePage.tsx:717-751).
claims.proposed_text: Choose the supplier from your clinic's enabled vendors. If it has its own order form, pick that form; otherwise use a Medipyxis standard form.

claims.claim: Save the order as a Draft, or Send Fax / Send Email to dispatch it to the vendor. On sending, the order moves to Submitted.

checks.note: email send would need to record the order as Submitted too

claims.finding: Send Fax records the order and sets Submitted (ensureOrderForSend :1265, recordFaxSend :1335; status written in ordersDmeService.ts:324). Send Email (handleSendVendorEmail, PatientOrdersDmePage.tsx:1371-1517) sends the email and shows a toast but never creates or updates the order — no status change. Product defect: emailed orders leave no Submitted record.
claims.proposed_text: Save the order as a draft, or click Send Fax to send it to the vendor; a faxed order moves to Submitted once the fax is accepted. Send Email emails the form but does not update the order's status.

claims.claim: The DME order appears in the DME tab with its status (Draft until sent, then Submitted → Received → Provisioned as the vendor works it).

checks.pattern: Received: "Provider has materials and is actively working it",

claims.claim: When results or confirmations come back, use Upload Results on the order.
claims.finding: Upload Results shows only on Provisioned orders and only raises a toast "Upload results"; nothing is uploaded (PatientOrdersDmePage.tsx:1606-1617). Product defect.
claims.proposed_text: Uploading results to an order is not available yet.

claims.claim: The order is linked to the patient record for tracking.
DME orders for Medicare beneficiaries must include an ICD-10 code, duration of need, and ordering provider NPI; Duration is required for Medicare compliance.
claims.finding: Regulatory statement, not product behaviour; the product does not enforce it (the standard DME form fields are free text and no required-field check for Medicare exists on the order path).

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: 'HCPCS code not shown' — change the category, HCPCS codes are category-scoped; 'Submit button disabled' — check Patient, Equipment Category, Item, Quantity, Duration, and ICD-10.
claims.finding: No Equipment Category, category-scoped HCPCS list, or Item field exists on either order surface (PatientOrdersDmePage.tsx, OrdersDMEVisit.tsx). Submit is disabled only while submitting or saving (PatientOrdersDmePage.tsx:4140).
claims.proposed_text: Remove these two troubleshooting rows. Keep "Patient not found — add the patient via Referral Intake".

claims.claim: Patient not found — add the patient via Referral Intake or the Patients module.
